newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The Bank of Greece has told the government that it must continue to insist on the reduction of inflation, intervene in the labour market, cut back on public expenditures and maintain a stable foreign exchange policy if it wants to achieve convergence.

--Farmers are to descend on Athens today in the hope that they will see Prime Minister Costas Simitis. Sources said yesterday that farmers would pick up and go home if the government made a "political commitment" on the cost of production of farm products. The government however reiterated yesterday that Simitis would only meet with the farmers once the roads were free.
--International prices have had an immediate effect on local fuel retail prices.

--The development ministry and insurance market are at odds over the rise in premiums: state run insurance companies with 40 percent of the market said they would increase premiums by no more than 10 percent while other firms are calling for 20.

--Industry has suffered losses equivalent to 0.7 of GDP due to the farmers' blockade, a Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) report has said. A survey of 530 industries shows a 56 billion drachma loss in production, 134 billion drachmas in deliveries and two billion drachmas in wages.
--The Bank of Greece predicts inflation at 7.5 percent by the end of the year, but is worried by the balance of payments.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said yesterday that state-run National, Commercial and Agicultural Banks Groups could expect to be strengthened with mergers with smaller banks.

--The central bank warns that the hard drachma policy will have to be supported by a more effective policy in other sectors of economic activity. Governor Lucas Papademos stresses structural measures, faster fiscal adjustment and a greater reduction in the cost of labour.

--Minoan Lines has ordered another vessel form Norway's Fosen, bringing the company's entire investment programme to 53 billion drachmas ($215 million). --A new European-wide electronic stock exchange will offer an alternative to the Greek market and give Greek investors the ability to widen their investment choices.
--The farmers' march on Athens is expected to be the grand finale to the 22-day blockade with hopes of a defusion of the crisis growing stronger.
--SEB criticises the budget as "more of the same" saying it does not address the issues of public spending or convergence targets.
--Scuffles portside as striking dockers prevent the disembarkation of passengers and lorries from foreign-flagged ferries.

--Extended privatisation will support the central aim of the budget - the reduction of the state deficit by 3.4 points, Papandoniou said in Parliament yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
